bullets.title: MU: Earnings Wed catalyst; buyside expects $30+ Aug EPS, SCAs, +10% options move
bullets.body: Micron reports F3Q26 Wed post-close with Street expecting $19.77B revenue, 81.2% gross margin, $20.83 EPS — all above guidance midpoints. Buyside consensus (~75%) expects new Strategic Customer Agreements; some see Aug Q EPS of $32-34 vs sell-side ~$25.59. Options pricing the largest implied earnings move (+10%) in a decade amid a Korea-driven semis selloff (KOSPI -10%, Hynix/Samsung each -12.5%), which is viewed as positioning cleanup rather than fundamental shift. MU also announced a multi-year strategic supply deal with Anthropic for HBM/DRAM/SSD.

bullets.title: Korea/semis selloff: levered ETF unwind amplifies move; AI capex story intact
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell ~10% Tuesday — triggering a circuit breaker — driven by Korean regulator caution on leveraged single-stock chip ETFs, stretched retail margin loans ($26B record), and pre-MU de-risking. JPM views Korea flash crashes as historically buyable (positive 3d/20d returns) and maintains constructive AI capex view with $5.5T estimate through 2030. Memory trade viewed as crowded positioning cleanup, not fundamental deterioration — DRAM spot pricing up 52% since January.

bullets.title: GOOGL: -5% on AI talent departures, Chinese model competition, capital rotation
bullets.body: Alphabet fell ~5% as DeepMind VP John Jumper (Nobel laureate, AlphaFold) departed to Anthropic and Noam Shazeer (Gemini co-lead) moved to OpenAI, fueling concerns Google has ceded AI momentum. China's GLM-5.2 model is now reportedly outperforming Gemini 3 Pro on SWE-bench at 1/6th the cost. Oppenheimer views talent departures as noise since Google can overpay for replacements and monetize frontier models via GCP; GOOGL remained on JPM Analyst Focus List.

bullets.title: AMZN: JPM raises PT to $330; Prime Day shifting $7-8B into 2Q, price hike likely 2027
bullets.body: JPM's Anmuth reiterates AMZN as Best Idea with PT $330 (32x 2027E GAAP EPS of $10.38). Prime delivers ~$1,440 annual value vs. $139 cost with 370M+ subscribers by end-2026; Prime Day (Jun 23-26) expected to shift $7-8B incremental revenue into Q2. A $20 price hike could generate ~$3B incremental annualized revenue but is now more likely in 2027 vs. 2026 given macro uncertainty. NiSource secured IURC approval for an Amazon data center partnership in Indiana.

bullets.title: MSFT: Bearish technicals (0/4 score); Azure/Copilot fundamentals remain constructive
bullets.body: 22V Research assigns MSFT a Technical Score of 0/4 — the worst rating — with the stock below its deteriorating 200-DMA since February, down 18%+ from its June high, and at a 6.5-year relative low vs. the S&P 500; a break below $350 support implies downside risk to $250. Contra-fundamentally, Wolfe pre-quiet period calls note Azure infrastructure efficiency driving growth and Copilot adoption expanding ARPU; CVX also signed a 20-year Microsoft agreement to power 2.7GW of data center capacity.

bullets.title: NFLX: -6% on META Instagram TV competition and alt-data showing sub-add weakness
bullets.body: Netflix dropped ~6% on two pressures: META expanding Instagram TV into long-form content competing directly with NFLX, and research showing US churn acceleration alongside watch time slipping from 100 min/day to 93 min/day (YouTube conversely rose from 87 to 99). NFLX now trades at ~20x NTM P/E, a 4-year low, with investor debate on short-cover levels.

bullets.title: CIEN: Citi Buy, $658 PT (43% upside); TAM doubling to $50B by 2029, EPS near-tripling
bullets.body: Citi reiterated Buy on Ciena with a $658 PT following Asia investor meetings. Revenue is growing ~32% (FY26 guide midpoint) with EPS expected to nearly triple; TAM seen doubling to ~$50B by 2029. Gross margins are targeted at the upper 40s with a path to 50%+. Citi values CIEN at 45x forward P/E on FY2028 EPS, reflecting a 2-year EPS CAGR of ~50%.

bullets.title: ACN: Mizuho cuts PT to $226; MS cuts to $130 on managed-services bookings decline
bullets.body: Accenture trimmed FY26 CC revenue growth guidance to +3-4% from +3-5%; bookings decelerated -3% CC y/y in F3Q26 with managed-services bookings down -15-16% y/y — well below the +4-5% investor expectation. MS cut its PT from $177 to $130 suggesting AI may be crowding out IT spend structurally. Mizuho cut to $226 (from $280) using 15x P/E on CY27E EPS. Partially offsetting: ACN raised its FY26 buyback program by $2B to $7.5B total (62% increase) and consulting bookings grew +11% y/y.

bullets.title: AMD: Citi Buy upgrade (6/12) gaining buyside traction; 2027E EPS $17 vs sell-side $13
bullets.body: Per Citi's semis roundtable, 50% of surveyed investors view the AMD Buy upgrade (initiated 6/12) as an incremental reason to buy, with buyside 2027E EPS at $17 vs. sell-side consensus $13. The GPU story has now eclipsed the mature CPU narrative as the core bull thesis.

bullets.title: MRVL: -9% presents defensive opportunity on pluggables/CPO ramp; TSEM +21% w/w on Marvell photonics deal
bullets.body: MRVL fell ~9% in the broad semis selloff but is viewed defensively given exposure to pluggable optics and coherent photonic integrated circuit (CPO) ramp scenarios; stock has underperformed memory peers. Separately, TSEM surged 21% week-over-week after announcing a collaboration with Marvell to ship over 5 million coherent photonic integrated circuits; realized vol hit 1-year highs at 110.1.

bullets.title: DIS: Goldman Buy, $163 PT; F3Q26 in-line, 2H26 acceleration expected
bullets.body: Goldman maintains Buy on Disney with a $163 price target, expecting an in-line F3Q26 print followed by 2H26 acceleration driven by Experiences segment EBIT growth of +13%, content cadence, and SVOD leverage. Goldman models 13% EPS CAGR through F2028 supported by operating leverage across segments.

bullets.title: APP: Gross spend potentially growing 50%+ y/y; ads platform now open to all users
bullets.body: Piper Sandler cites CloudX data suggesting APP gross spend could be growing north of 50% y/y, with mobile gaming showing strongest y/y growth in app-ads.txt connections in 2+ years (ex-Scopely). TTWO mobile studios saw +30% y/y growth in the same metric. Separately, JPM notes APP's ads platform opened to all users without referral, though monetization impact needs clarity by Q4 2026.

bullets.title: AFRM: Mizuho raises PT to $100; Walmart shoppers prefer Affirm 2x over Klarna
bullets.body: Mizuho proprietary survey of ~450 Walmart shoppers shows Affirm preferred over Klarna overall (41% vs 36%) and 2x preferred among online-first users (24% vs 12%), despite Klarna being the exclusive BNPL partner for 1+ year. Mizuho raises PT to $100 (from prior) and rates Outperform at current $72.20, valuing at 6x CY27E net revenue vs. 5x peer average.

bullets.title: ROKU: Acquired by Fox at $160/share per ChatJTP report
bullets.body: Fox is reportedly acquiring Roku at $160/share; CEO Anthony Wood is said to be willing to sell after the stock traded in a $45-100 range since 2022 despite COVID-era highs of ~$400. A Tubi + Roku Channel combination would represent 5.2% of U.S. TV video hours. Netflix has already passed on bidding and viable second bidders are viewed as narrow.

bullets.title: DLR: $1.61B in transactions; Citi maintains Buy, MS Equal-weight, prefers EQIX
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced a $475M acquisition of a Kansas City land site with 600MW utility power (up to 2GW at full delivery), a $650M increase in Teraco ownership to 77%, and a $485M acquisition of Columbia Capital — issuing 6.3M shares (~2% dilution) at $197.54. Citi maintains Buy with room for multiple expansion; Morgan Stanley maintains Equal-weight at $215 PT and prefers OW-rated EQIX for retail exposure and pricing power.

bullets.title: MSFT/NOW/HUBS/TEAM: Pre-quiet period takeaways; HUBS cut to $220, TEAM to $120
bullets.body: Wolfe pre-quiet period calls: MSFT tone incrementally positive on Azure efficiency and Copilot ARPU; NOW constructive with AI Control Tower demand; TWLO very positive on Voice AI. HUBS faces near-term NNARR headwinds from April GTM changes and shifting ROI demands — PT cut 27% to $220. TEAM confident in Cloud but DC revenue seen declining ~15% in FY27 — PT cut 14% to $120.

bullets.title: ORCL: Cut 13% of workforce (~21,000 roles) amid AI-driven restructuring
bullets.body: Oracle ended FY26 with 141K employees, down ~21K (-13%) year-over-year amid AI-driven restructuring. RPO duration skew is positive near-term. Multiple sources confirm ORCL is also adding 1GW of data center capacity, and data center moratoriums have not emerged as a macro headwind for well-planned projects.

bullets.title: TSLA: European registrations +107.9% y/y in May; under NHTSA investigation
bullets.body: Tesla's EU+EFTA+UK new car registrations jumped 107.9% y/y in May 2026, outpacing BYD (+136.6%) and the broader market (+3.6%). Separately, Tesla remains under NHTSA investigation for a crash involving its driver-assistance system.

bullets.title: SNAP: SPECS AR glasses unveiled; investor critiques on price and bulkiness
bullets.body: Snap unveiled its SPECS AR glasses, with investor reaction focusing on concerns around price, bulkiness, and lack of live demos. The first consumer release form factor is reportedly less bulky than competing mixed-reality devices. Snap also spun off its internal gen-AI video team into a separate company (Dotmo) due to costs.

bullets.title: MDB: Partners with xAI; Databricks positioned as enterprise AI control layer competing with MSFT/AMZN/ORCL
bullets.body: MongoDB announced a partnership with xAI. Roth's Databricks AI Summit recap highlights Databricks at $5.4B ARR (80% YoY growth) positioning as the governance/control layer for enterprise AI — with custom RL-trained models matching frontier models at far lower cost — creating increasing competitive tension with Microsoft (Azure Databricks + Fabric), AMZN, and ORCL.
